fields.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not, either before
or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on
any of the following types of criminal records:
fields.note: The summary tracks sections 4-12: the pre-offer inquiry ban and its exceptions, barred record types, post-offer limits, withdrawal standard, individualized assessment, notice and records request, fee disclosure, advertising and dissemination limits, drug/alcohol test ban, immunity, Division-only enforcement, mediation, penalties and remedies.

fields.quoted_span:
an amount not to exceed $1,000 if the housing
provider has not committed any prior violation within the five-year period
fields.note: The lookback periods (6/4/1 years), the lifetime list of serious offenses, the 30-day request and free 10-day response, and the $1,000/$5,000/$10,000 penalty tiers all match sections 5 and 12.

fields.quoted_span: seventh month next following the date of enactment
fields.note: Section 14 sets the effective date and the act was approved June 18, 2021. The first day of the seventh month after that is January 1, 2022.

fields.quoted_span:
This act shall take effect on the first day of the
seventh month next following the date of enactment
fields.note: The document is the enacted chapter law with a passed effective date. It does not itself say the law is currently in force, so that status is inferred.

fields.quoted_span: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
fields.note: The definition of 'rental dwelling unit' covers units offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes and excludes units in owner-occupied premises of four or fewer units.
The document's codification for section 4 (application process) matches the primary citation. The aliases cover the other codified sections, 46:8-52 to -64, and P.L.2021, c.110.
